clearedSpotChecks.check: When the PoolManager runs as native code on a Monad validator (v0.16.7 compile rule, threshold 10,240 + 32 x 24,009 = 778,528 gas, release dates and first blocks of 2026-10-22 and 2026-11-26).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the v0.16.7 sources from raw.githubusercontent.com. vm.cpp lines 141-189 run native code when the varcode holds it, fall back to the interpreter only when compilation failed for this revision, compile at once while the cache is cold, and otherwise call async_compile once intercode_gas_used reaches max_code_size. x86.hpp lines 53-64 return offset + shl<5>(bytecode_size), types.hpp lines 141-142 set the offset to bin<10 * 1024>, and varcode_cache.hpp lines 29-33 set the warm mark at three quarters of 2^22 kB. compiler.cpp lines 106-140 show async_compile can skip a job when the queue is over its soft limit; that only delays compilation and does not change any result. The releases page lists v0.16.7 on mainnet on 2026-11-26 and v0.16.5 on 2026-10-22. eth_getBlockByNumber on rpc.monad.xyz gives 2026-11-25 23:59:59 for block 125,426,596 and 2026-11-26 00:00:00 for 125,426,597, and 2026-10-21 23:59:59 for 115,463,612 and 2026-10-22 00:00:00 for 115,463,613. The per-validator restart time is unpublished, as the item says.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Replay of 3,042 mined PoolManager transactions since v0.16.7 in pyevm, with 3 frame mismatches explained as out of gas or uncovered value, logs equal to eth_getLogs and storage equal to the diff-mode post state and eth_getStorageAt.
clearedSpotChecks.note: replay-summary.json records 3,042 transactions, 3,039 ok and 3 frame-mismatch, logs equal in 3,041 and storage equal in 3,042; replay-mismatches.json holds exactly 3 rows. I traced the first mismatch, 0x58fc80e6..., with debug_traceTransaction callTracer on rpc.monad.xyz: the last unlock frame reverts and its inner swap frame (0xf3cd914c) ends with error out of gas after using all of its 0x1bc5b gas, which is the gas case the gasless reference does not model. eth_getStorageAt on slot 0x01e7b865...d6e6d of the PoolManager returns 0x...01f4000000fb17f7...c842fd35991a0611 at block 125,517,342 and 0x...01f4000000fb17f8...cd9fdb167eb0b698 at block 125,517,343, the second equal to the replay's written value. The link from tracing nodes to consensus holds: cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7 selects InterpreterOnly when call tracing is on and Dual otherwise, so traced and read results come from the interpreter on nodes that follow the same chain as native validators. The item's 336 transactions with a failed PoolManager frame and the summary's failedFrames 360 count different things (transactions and frames) and do not conflict.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Which of the 913 compiled IR blocks mined transactions entered (660 entered, 253 not: 15 unreachable, 40 revert, 70 dispatch and decoding, 128 value), and that all 238 reachable unentered blocks were entered by native code in the cycle 28 clang harness.
clearedSpotChecks.note: notentered-classified.json lists 253 blocks with class counts value 128, dispatch-decode 70, revert 40, unreachable 15, and replay-summary.json gives 660 entered. cycles/028 summary.json gives 913 blocks at both 0.16.5 and 0.16.7 with 898 entered by some harness set and 15 not entered, so the 238 reachable blocks are covered by the clang harness. The residual risk is that the 128 value blocks have no mined native execution and the gcc emitter validators run has not executed them; the unit records this as its own medium lead and does not claim it cleared. No mined word in this unit gives an ordinary account a producer difference to use.
